index_metaTitle: DartPDF: private, local PDF editor for every device
index_metaDesc: Edit PDFs locally on desktop, mobile, or web. Annotate, run OCR, fill forms, add drawn or digital signatures, redact, compare, and edit text. No uploads.
hero_h1:
Free, local PDF editor
for every device.
hero_sub: Open a PDF, mark it up, run OCR on scanned pages, fill forms, sign, redact, compare, and make small text or image edits. DartPDF runs on desktop, mobile, and web, and your documents stay on your device unless you choose to share them.
hero_note: Free and open source. No account. No uploads.
hero_shotAlt: The DartPDF editor showing a PDF with annotation tools, page thumbnails, and a color palette.
feat_h2: The PDF jobs you actually need.
feat_intro: Mark up a file, run OCR, fill forms, move pages, compare versions, or fix a small mistake without sending the PDF to a server.
featAnnotate_d: Highlight text, draw with ink, add shapes, notes, and stamps.
featForms_d: Fill existing fields or add new text fields, checkboxes, and buttons.
featSign_d: Place a drawn signature, or add a certificate-backed digital signature.
featRedact_d: Remove sensitive text and images from the file, not just from view.
featEdit_d: Fix small text runs or drop in images without rebuilding the file.
featPages_d: Reorder, delete, split, and export pages to a new file.
featSearch_d: Search selectable text and copy it from the page.
featOcr_d: Turn scanned pages into searchable, selectable PDFs.
featCompare_d: Check two versions side by side.
privBand_h2: Your documents never leave your device.
privBand_p: DartPDF has no servers, analytics, or ads. It works with files locally, including OCR, and shares a document only when you choose a destination.
dl_intro: We'll show the best downloads for this device. Every other platform is still one tap away.
dlWin_portable: Prefer not to install? Get the Windows portable build that runs from anywhere.
dl_freeNote: Free and open source. Other builds (.zip, .tar.gz) on GitHub Releases.
dev_h2: A pure-Dart PDF engine you can use too.
dev_p: The engine uses Dart instead of PDFium or native bindings, so it runs anywhere Dart and Flutter do. The packages are Apache-2.0 licensed and published on pub.dev. Read the Flutter PDF editor overview for benchmarks and a comparison with commercial SDKs.
engCos_d: PDF object model, parser, filters, xref
foot_tagline: A private, local PDF editor for every device.
foot_oss: Free and open source under Apache-2.0.
pp_metaDesc: DartPDF does its work entirely on your device and does not collect, transmit, or share any personal data.
pp_lede: DartPDF is a PDF viewer and editor published by Railway Engineering Solutions Pty Ltd ("we", "us"). This policy explains how the app handles your information. The short version: DartPDF does its work entirely on your device and does not collect, transmit, or share any personal data.
pp_p_collect: Nothing. DartPDF has no analytics, no advertising, no accounts, and no backend servers. We do not collect, log, or transmit any personal information, usage data, or device identifiers.
pp_p_docs1: PDFs you open, edit, annotate, sign, or save are processed locally on your device only. Their contents are never uploaded to us or to any third party. When you choose to share or export a document, it goes only to the destination you pick (for example, another app via the system share sheet, or a file location you select).
pp_p_docs2: OCR also runs locally. Native builds may download OCR model files on first use, then recognition runs on your device. The web build downloads browser OCR model and runtime files on first use, then runs recognition in the browser. Your PDF pages and recognized text are not sent to a DartPDF OCR server.
pp_p_perms: DartPDF requests access to files only so it can open the PDFs you choose and save your changes back. This access is used solely to perform the action you requested and for no other purpose.
pp_p_prefs: Settings such as your theme, recent-file list, and tool styles are stored locally on your device using the operating system's standard preference storage. They never leave your device and are removed when you uninstall the app or clear its data.
pp_p_third: DartPDF does not embed third-party analytics, advertising, or tracking SDKs. The app may open external links (such as its source-code repository) in your browser when you explicitly tap them; those destinations have their own privacy policies.
pp_p_children: DartPDF is a general-purpose productivity tool and does not knowingly collect any information from anyone, including children.
pp_p_changes: If this policy changes, we will update the "Last updated" date above and post the revised policy at the same URL.
sp_metaDesc: Get help with DartPDF - contact support, report a bug, and find answers to common questions.
sp_lede: Need a hand with DartPDF? We're happy to help. The fastest way to reach us is by email, and we usually reply within a couple of business days.
sp_bug_label: Report a bug or request a feature: github.com/ben-milanko/dart-pdf/issues
sp_contact_note: When you write in, it helps to include your device and OS version, the DartPDF version (Settings → About), and the steps that led to the problem. If a specific PDF is involved and you're able to share it, that speeds things up - but it's never required.
sp_faq1: Where do my changes save? Edits - markup, form fills, signatures, redaction, page changes, and text/image edits - save back to the original PDF on your device. Nothing is uploaded; there's no account or sync.
sp_faq2: How do I open a PDF? Open DartPDF and pick a file, open a PDF from the Files app, send one to DartPDF from another app's share sheet, or drag and drop a file onto the window.
sp_faq3: Can I open password-protected PDFs? Yes. DartPDF prompts for the password and opens encrypted files for viewing and editing.
sp_faq4: How does OCR work? Optical character recognition runs entirely on your device. On first use the app downloads the recognition model, then all processing happens locally - your pages are never sent to a server.
sp_faq5: Is my data private? Yes. DartPDF has no analytics, no ads, no accounts, and no servers. See the privacy policy for the details.
sp_stuck_p: Email ben.milanko@protonmail.com and describe what you were trying to do. We read every message.
sdk_metaTitle: Flutter PDF editor: open-source Dart package | DartPDF
sdk_metaDesc: Add a complete PDF editor to Flutter with dart_pdf_editor. View, annotate, fill forms, sign, redact, edit text, and save on every Flutter platform.
sdk_hero_h1: A complete Flutter PDF editor, written entirely in Dart.
sdk_hero_sub: Add dart_pdf_editor to edit existing PDFs inside a Flutter app. The drop-in editor views, annotates, fills forms, signs, redacts, edits text, manages pages, and saves changes back to PDF. It uses one Dart engine on iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux, and web, with no PDFium or platform views. Apache-2.0, on pub.dev.
sdk_feat_h2: The commercial-SDK feature set, open source.
sdk_feat_intro: Viewing, annotating, forms, signing, redaction, page management, text editing, and OCR. In other words, the things apps actually license a PDF SDK for.
sdkFeatViewer_d: Zoom and pan with fit modes, deep-zoom detail rendering, text selection, full-text search, links, outlines, dark mode, and theming.
sdkFeatAnnot_d: Markup, pressure-sensitive ink, shapes, callouts, notes, stamps, and measurement tools, all with generated appearance streams. Select, move, resize, rotate, copy/paste, undo/redo.
sdkFeatForms_d: Fill AcroForm text, checkbox, radio, and choice fields with regenerated appearances. You can also author fields: create, rename, retype, delete, flatten.
sdkFeatSign_d: Sign and validate up to PAdES B-LTA with RFC 3161 timestamps and long-term validation. Output validates in pyHanko, OpenSSL, and poppler.
sdkFeatRedact_d: True redaction per the PDF spec: covered text and images are removed from the file bytes, not painted over.
sdkFeatText_d: Rewrite existing page text in place with width-compensated metrics, and reflow whole paragraphs when the line count changes.
sdkFeatPages_d: Reorder, delete, merge across documents, and split to new files, with drag-and-drop thumbnail UI included.
sdkFeatOcr_d: Pluggable engines add an invisible, selectable text layer to scans: on-device PP-OCR via ONNX, or any HTTP OCR service, including on Flutter web.
sdkFeatParse_d: Encrypted files (RC4/AES), broken real-world PDFs, CCITT/JBIG2/JPEG 2000 images, and ICC color, with conformance pinned against the Ghent suite and the PDF.js test corpus.
sdk_perf_h2: Pure Dart is not a compromise on speed.
sdk_perf_p1: On a real-world corpus of 49 files and 255 pages (CAD drawings, scans, reports, forms), the parse and content-stream interpreter runs about 1.9× faster than PDFium, the C++ engine Chrome uses. Full Flutter rasterization is currently about 2× slower end to end; the gap is image decoding and GPU raster, not the interpreter.
sdk_perf_p2: The benchmark harness diffs dart-pdf against PDFium file by file, so you can check the numbers yourself.
sdk_bench_title: ms per page, lower is better
sdk_bench_note: Scale 2, PDFium via pypdfium2. Methodology and per-file results in the repo's benchmark/ directory.
sdk_cmp_h2: How it compares to commercial PDF SDKs.
sdk_cmp_intro: Nutrient (formerly PSPDFKit) and Syncfusion are mature, well-supported commercial products. The difference is architecture and licensing: dart-pdf is one open-source Dart engine on every platform Flutter ships to.
sdk_cmp_signA: Sign + validate, PAdES up to B-LTA
sdk_cmp_note: Vendor capabilities summarized from their public documentation as of July 2026. Always check the vendors' current docs. No performance comparisons are made against commercial SDKs.
sdk_pkg_h2: Strictly layered, use what you need.
sdk_pkg_intro: The Flutter widgets sit on three pure-Dart packages that run on the VM, in CLIs and servers, and on the web. There is no Flutter dependency below the widget layer.
sdkPkgEditor_d: Flutter PDF viewer and editing UI: PdfEditorView, PdfReader, tools, panels, forms, theming.
sdkPkgDoc_d: Document semantics: page tree, annotations, AcroForm, digital signatures, incremental-save editor.
sdkPkgGfx_d: Content-stream interpreter, font engine, ICC color, and text extraction. Renders to any device.
sdkPkgCos_d: The PDF file format itself: parser, filters, encryption, xref machinery, serializer, crypto.
sdkPkgOndevice_d: Optional on-device OCR engine: downloads a small PP-OCR model once, then runs offline.
sdkPkgVlm_d: Optional HTTP OCR engine for web, mobile, and desktop. Point it at any service that returns text boxes.
